properties.title: GlyTwin: Enhancing Digital Twin for Glucose Control in Type 1 Diabetes using Patient-Centric Counterfactual Treatments

properties.version_basis: PDF identified by SHA-256 against assignments.json; title page read.

properties.description: Counterfactual explanation search over a glycemic outcome classifier to suggest behavioral changes, evaluated on a new free-living T1D dataset.

An MLP classifier of post-meal hyperglycemia and a saliency-guided iterative counterfactual search that perturbs carbohydrate, bolus, bolus timing and pre-meal glucose within preference-weighted bounds.

properties.algorithm: Fully connected binary classifier of hyperglycemia from eleven features

properties.population: adults with type 1 diabetes on automated insulin delivery

properties.description: AZT1D, 50 adults with T1D at Mayo Clinic Arizona, about 26 days each, 2672 meal samples with 85/15 subject-level split
Counterfactual validity, simulator validity, nearest neighbor test, proximity, sparsity, violations and plausibility against four baselines over 4 trials
properties.split_role: random 85/15 split at subject and sample level

properties.algorithm: XGBoost outcome simulator used for validity

properties.summary: GlyTwin bi-delta-t validity by XGBoost simulator = 0.858

metric_results.metric: GlyTwin bi-delta-t validity by XGBoost simulator

relation_assertions.rationale: Counterfactual behavioral alternatives are compared by simulated and historical outcome checks, with no dynamics model or controller.

capability_assessments.rationale: The system searches the inputs of a static meal-level binary MLP hyperglycemia classifier to produce counterfactual behavioral adjustments, with no persistent evolving state (state.persistent absent/not reported), no temporal transition dynamics (dynamics.temporal absent/not reported), no rollout, and no world-model representation objective. Consequently, it does not meet core world-model membership or L0, and is classified as not_world_model (consistent with entities[].properties.world_model_status and legacy_disagreements). Counterfactual suggestions are evaluated only by an associational XGBoost simulator, LoopInsighT1, and a historical k-NN proxy, and the authors explicitly note they are not clinically tested.

legacy_cells.B: GlyTwin: Enhancing Digital Twin for Glucose Control in Type 1 Diabetes using Patient-Centric Counterfactual Treatments
legacy_cells.S: Which changes to meal-related inputs would change the classifier's predicted postprandial outcome from hyperglycemia to normoglycemia?
legacy_cells.T: 50 individuals with T1D using Tandem T:SLIM X2 insulin pumps and Dexcom G6 Pro CGMs; free-living recordings for approximately 26 days per subject.
legacy_cells.U: Individuals with T1D and physicians (the stated stakeholders).
legacy_cells.V: Selecting proposed changes to carbohydrate intake, insulin bolus, bolus-meal timing, and pre-meal glucose features to shift the predicted class to normoglycemia; clinical benefit was not tested.
legacy_cells.AI: Structured tabular features: age; gender; ethnicity; A1C; carbohydrate size; total bolus; bolus-meal interval (Δt); device mode; total basal; pre-meal BGL slope; pre-meal BGL.
legacy_cells.AN: Missing values were handled during preprocessing; records with missing data were removed.
legacy_cells.BD: Modified features: carbohydrate size (grams), total bolus (insulin units), bolus-meal interval Δt (minutes), and pre-meal blood glucose (mg/dL).
legacy_cells.BF: Modifiable feature ranges were personalized by subject; pre-meal blood glucose was constrained to 100–170 mg/dL. Target confidence γ=0.6 and maximum iterations N=400.
legacy_cells.CA: One compute node with 12 CPU cores, 24 GiB RAM, and one NVIDIA L40 GPU.
legacy_cells.CB: Counterfactual generation runtime: approximately 5.2 seconds on average per CF.
legacy_cells.CX: Counterfactual consistency was assessed using a real-data-trained XGBoost emulator, LoopInsighT1 physiological simulation, and a k=7 nearest-neighbor test against historical cases. Table IV reports classifier validity 0.858 for GlyTwin bi-Δt and 0.858 for one-Δt; LoopInsighT1 validity 0.9 and NN test 0.873±0.004 are reported for one-Δt. These are predictive/simulated checks, not clinical or causally identified treatment-effect validation.
legacy_cells.FN: Reported results (source excerpt): Results show that GlyTwin outperforms state-of-the-art methods for generating counterfactual explanations with 85.8% valid explanations and 87.3% effectiveness in preventing hyperglycemia when compared against historical data.
legacy_cells.FX: Complete extracted text read, PDF pp. 1–17: title/abstract, introduction, problem statement and solution, data collection/preprocessing, methods and experimental setup, Tables I–VI, results, discussion/ablations, limitations, future validation plans, conclusion, and supplementary materials. Main cohort and results tables were legible; some equations and table layout/text in the extraction are OCR/formula-corrupted. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: The implementation is a static MLP classifier with iterative counterfactual feature perturbations, not a temporal state-transition world model; exclude as static prediction without state evolution. The abstract claims counterfactual treatments (AA=L3 claim), but the observed evaluation does not establish causal treatment effects. Evidence maturity is retrospective internal validation (R2: random 85/15 subject- and datapoint-level split); the paper explicitly reports no clinical testing. Some extracted equations and supplementary table layout are OCR/formula-corrupted, but the cohort and primary results tables used here were readable. Evidence QA: 6/33 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (18.2%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 30 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 3 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: Targeted 2026-11-22 review resolved remaining visual-inventory and bibliography-entry gaps on the same hash-pinned PDF. Prior text/visual work is reused with original attribution; details and actual new page receipts are in verification.json. Bibliographies were read as entries only; cited full texts and external videos/code were not inspected.
The legacy row was read from the root workbook (read only). Saved API drafts for A14 were not opened.
Schema validity and quote occurrence do not establish semantic correctness. One reviewer pass, no independent human review.
Main p11 Table VI and adjacent prose disagree on proximity/runtime ranges; numerical records were not silently changed. Supplement numbering restarts at Figure 1/Table I.
notes: GlyTwin is a saliency-guided counterfactual search over an MLP that classifies post-meal hyperglycemia (accuracy 82.63 percent, AUC 0.837) trained on 2672 meal samples from 50 adults with T1D. Counterfactual validity is 0.858 by an XGBoost simulator (itself 80.23 percent accurate), 0.9 by LoopInsighT1 and 0.873 by a nearest neighbor historical check, above DiCE, NICE, CFNOW and Optbinning. It carries no state or dynamics, so it is not a world model. Classified not_world_model, not core, R2 with R1 simulator evidence. Source points: abstract effectiveness is a neighbor proxy, tuning on the test set, sparsity text conflicts with Table IV, no clinical validation.
